RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Raising the panel's gender composition will undermine your professional credibility. In secondary education, all-female panels are common and do not indicate bias; demographic makeup alone carries no legal or procedural weight. 

While your administrative credentials may look stronger on paper, principal appointments rely heavily on interview evaluations, leadership vision, references, and institutional fit. 

Do not allege sex discrimination based on demographics. Instead, send a polite follow-up requesting your written feedback and evaluation scores against the objective criteria. If the formal documentation reveals clear procedural violations or arbitrary scoring, you can challenge the decision strictly on the merits of the process rather than the composition of the panel.
